function.name: calculate_electric_current
function.description: Calculate the electric current through a conductor given voltage and resistance. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

voltage.description: The voltage across the conductor in Volts. This is a float type value.

resistance.description: The resistance of the conductor in Ohms. This is a float type value.

conductance.description: The conductance of the conductor in Siemens. Optional if resistance is provided. Default: 0.3 This is a float type value.

message.content: Electricity wasn’t discovered by a single individual—it emerged from the collective work of many scientists over centuries. Early observations date back to ancient Greece (Thales of Miletus noted static electricity), while significant advances were made by figures such as William Gilbert (who coined the term “electricity”), Benjamin Franklin (the lightning‑rod experiments), Alessandro Volta (invented the voltaic pile), and Michael Faraday (discovered electromagnetic induction). Each built on previous discoveries, leading to our modern understanding of electrical phenomena.
